content.title: Tailor-made Antigua and Barbuda Holidays 2026/2027
content.text: What are Antigua and Barbuda famous for? Beautiful beaches abound in Antigua and Barbuda, and with 365 to choose from, there’s one for every day of the year (fancy a year-long sabbatical, anyone?). Some are ideal for relaxation, while others are better suited to family days out or water sports, but they all boast the powder-soft sands and turquoise waters of paradise. What is the food like in Antigua and Barbuda? Antiguan cuisine is a melting pot of Caribbean and Guyanese flavours, centred around fresh fish, aromatic spices and locally-grown fruit. Common dishes include: Ducana, a dumpling made from sweet potato, grated coconut, sugar, spices and flour, combined with briny saltfish. Pepperpot, stewed meat flavoured with cassareep (a thick syrup made from the cassava root), hot peppers and cinnamon. Fungee, savoury cornmeal. Butter bread, a soft bread eaten with cheese or sardines. The islands are also famed for Antigua black pineapples, which are one of the sweetest and least acidic varieties of the prickly fruit. They can be eaten on their own as a simple snack or served with honey and a squeeze of lime juice. What is the drink like in Antigua and Barbuda? Popular drinks include rum punch, a refreshing cocktail made with local rum, lime juice, sugar and bitters, and served over ice. Wadadli beer, Antigua’s national brew, is another local favourite. Soft drinks include sweet tropical juices made from mango, raspberry and passion fruit, as well as ginger beer and coconut milk. Do you tip in Antigua and Barbuda? Tipping isn’t required, but it’s customary to tip between 10 and 15% if you’re satisfied with the service. What etiquette rules do I need to know? Locals have a conservative attitude towards dressing, so it’s best to avoid wearing revealing clothing or beach attire to restaurants. Dressing in camouflage clothing is considered an offence. Attitudes towards the LGBTQ+ community are conservative throughout the Caribbean, and public displays of affection are uncommon.
